column3: Close to the Hebrew; “Spice” is rendered “balsam,” and “become drunk” as “imbibe deeply.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The sound of my beloved knocking” is rendered “A voice! My beloved was knocking,” and “filled with dew” as “drenched with dew.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Tunic” is rendered “dress,” and NASB adds “again.”
“From the hole” is rendered “through the opening,” and “my inward parts were turbulent on him” as “my feelings were aroused for him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Flowing myrrh” is rendered “liquid myrrh.”
“My being went out” is rendered “My heart went out to him,” adding “to him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Bruised” is rendered “wounded,” “garment” as “shawl,” and “the watchmen of the walls” as “The guardsmen of the walls.”
Close to the Hebrew; “What will you tell him? That I am weak of love” is rendered “As to what you will tell him: For I am lovesick.”
Close to the Hebrew; “How is your beloved more than a beloved” is rendered “What kind of beloved is your beloved.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Conspicuous” is rendered “Outstanding.”
“Curls” (a word of uncertain meaning) is rendered “clusters of dates,” and NASB adds “like” and “And black.”
“Sitting on fullness” is rendered “reposed in their setting.” The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “Spice” is rendered “balsam,” and “towers” as “Banks.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Chrysolite” is rendered “beryl,” “his lower parts” as “His abdomen,” and “a plate of ivory” as “carved ivory.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Marble” is rendered “alabaster.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Sweetnesses” is rendered “full of sweetness,” and “all of him [is] desirableness” as “he is wholly desirable.”
